authority.non_authority_statement: This active inventory grants no accepted-decision, implementation, or activation authority.

lifecycle.terminal_handling: Remove resolved, rejected, or superseded records in the same bounded package that records their accepted ADR, canonical rationale, or explicit rejection; preserve history in Git and linked Issues rather than in a second permanent archive.

records.blocking_owner_question: Accept ADR 0035 Option A: use a TUF-based role-separated updater repository with stable/beta channel delegation and private signing authority outside the Laravel web runtime, or select Option B (a custom single signed manifest envelope)?
records.decision_question: What cryptographic trust and publication model should first-party Oteryn client updates use before launcher/updater launch claims?

DERIVED: The current browser-oriented Download Center cannot safely become updater trust authority merely by exposing is_current, an immutable URL or an administrator-supplied digest.
A secure first-party updater needs signed freshness and rollback/mix-and-match resistance in addition to immutable artifact bytes.
PROVEN: Downloads already defines stable and beta channels plus explicit platform and architecture variants.
Issue 948 and PR 966 enforce machine-testable immutable artifact references while preserving the no-fetch and supplied-checksum boundary.
Canonical portal architecture explicitly leaves minimum-version, mandatory-update, updater-manifest and publisher-provenance policy unresolved.
UNKNOWN: Exact external updater implementation, maintained TUF library choice, metadata serialization and protected signing infrastructure were not inspected in this Platform-only task.
Exact numerical metadata expiry intervals and signing-key custody ceremony require implementation and operational evidence.

options.description: Use The Update Framework role/freshness/version model, separate stable and beta delegated target authority, offline threshold Root custody, protected release signing outside Laravel, and an authenticated Oteryn policy target for minimum/mandatory/revocation semantics.
options.title: TUF-based role-separated updater repository
trade_offs: Strong standard rollback, freeze and mix-and-match defenses with explicit key roles and rotation semantics.
More release metadata, key operations, bootstrap/profile work and client integration complexity than one custom signature envelope.

options.description: Define one Oteryn-specific signed manifest carrying artifact identity, generation, expiry, minimum-version, mandatory-update and revocation policy while pinning publisher trust anchors in the client.
options.title: Custom single signed manifest envelope
trade_offs: Smaller operational and implementation surface for the first release.
Oteryn must design and maintain its own replay, rollback, freeze, consistency, threshold and key-recovery protocol.

options.description: Use the current HTTPS Download Center plus immutable artifact URLs and supplied SHA-256 as updater policy.
options.title: HTTPS and checksum status quo
trade_offs: Does not provide signed publisher provenance or a freshness/replay policy and turns mutable web state into update authority.

options.description: Give the Laravel web application an online private signing key so it can generate trusted manifests dynamically.
options.title: Web-runtime manifest signing
trade_offs: Simple coupling between administrator publication and signed metadata.
A web compromise becomes software-signing compromise and violates the proposed least-privilege key-custody boundary.

records.problem_statement: First-party automatic updates need one publisher-authenticated, freshness-bounded and rollback-resistant policy source; the current Download Center was deliberately built as browser metadata and checksum presentation rather than software-signing authority.
records.recommendation: Adopt Option A. Reuse TUF's role, version, expiry and delegation model; keep private signing authority outside Laravel and represent Oteryn-specific minimum/mandatory/revocation rules in a TUF-authenticated policy target.
records.title: First-party client distribution and updater trust boundary
